gap: None of the results ChatGPT got turns a NAS's network rating into the bitrate Infuse needs. A gigabit NAS measured at about 112 MB/s (896–944 Mbit/s) has roughly 7× the headroom of the 128 Mbit/s Ultra HD Blu-ray maximum. The Apple TV 4K's own port is only Gigabit Ethernet, and the 64 GB model has no Ethernet port at all, so a 2.5GbE NAS gives no benefit to a single Infuse stream.
standout_why: I opened Firecore's 'Streaming From a Mac, PC, or NAS' (cited) and itechguides' Infuse setup guide (top result). Firecore covers protocols (SMB, NFS, WebDAV and others), the SMB-version setting and SMB3 encryption slowing playback. It says nothing about Ethernet or Wi-Fi, bitrate, 4K/remux or NAS hardware. itechguides only says to 'check the connection, file bitrate, and server capability' and gives no figures. ChatGPT's answer says 'Gigabit Ethernet' is enough but never shows the arithmetic, and never mentions that the 64 GB Apple TV 4K has no Ethernet port. I did not open firecore.com/infuse.
decides: It confirms the pick: buy the cheapest 1GbE box with SMB/NFS (Synology DS124 or DS223j, TerraMaster F2-212, UGREEN DH2300). It rules out paying more for 2.5GbE (UGREEN DXP2800, Asustor AS1102TL) just for Infuse, because the Apple TV caps the link at 1 Gb/s. Owners of the 64 GB Wi-Fi-only Apple TV 4K have Wi-Fi 6 as their only link, so for them the router matters more than the NAS port. A second normalisation note for the page: makers' low power figures are 'HDD hibernation' numbers, not idle numbers. Synology lists 3.44 W (DS124) and 4 W (DS223j) for hibernation, while ocinside measured 9–11 W idle on the DH2300. Compare idle against idle.

findings.label: Apple TV 4K (3rd gen) network ports
findings.value: Wi-Fi + Ethernet 128 GB: Gigabit Ethernet + Wi-Fi 6 (2x2 MIMO); Wi-Fi 64 GB: no Ethernet port, Wi-Fi 6 only
findings.note: Apple lists Ethernet only under the 128 GB Wi-Fi + Ethernet model. The fastest wired link any current Apple TV 4K can use is 1 Gb/s.

findings.label: Ultra HD Blu-ray maximum data rate (worst case for a 4K remux)
findings.value: 108 Mbit/s (66 GB dual-layer), 128 Mbit/s (100 GB triple-layer)
findings.source_title: 4K Blu-ray discs: BDA agrees standards for next-generation discs (What Hi-Fi?, 18 Feb 2015)
findings.note: What Hi-Fi? attributes the figures to the BDA's Victor Matsuda. A remux copies the disc stream, so 128 Mbit/s is the ceiling Infuse has to pull over SMB/NFS.

findings.label: Measured network throughput (iperf3, 1GbE)
findings.note: Unit conversion: 112 MB/s × 8 = 896 Mbit/s, which is 7.0× the 128 Mbit/s disc maximum. The reviewer's own 944 Mbit/s works out to 7.4×. The two figures they give don't match (944/8 = 118 MB/s), so the page should use the lower one. Blackmagic sequential writes were over 100 MB/s.

findings.label: Measured wall power
findings.value: 9–11 W idle; 12–13 W copying over the network; 15–17 W at 100% CPU stress; about 1 W when powered off
findings.note: Measured with a Shelly Plug S, which the reviewer calls 'not super accurate'. Two drives in RAID-1. The current page's '9.5 W idle' falls inside this range.

findings.label: Maker specs relevant to Infuse
findings.value: 1× 1GbE (MTU limit 1500); SMB, NFS, AFP, FTP, WebDAV; Realtek RTD1619B 4-core 1.7 GHz, 1 GB DDR4; 10.69 W access / 3.44 W HDD hibernation; 19.0 dB(A) idle; 2-year warranty (extendable to 4)
findings.note: The 3.44 W figure is with the drives spun down (hibernation), not idle. The power footnote does not name the test drives. The noise test used Synology SATA HDDs.

findings.label: Maker specs relevant to Infuse
findings.value: 1× 1GbE (MTU limit 1500); SMB1/2/3, NFSv3/v4/v4.1; Realtek RTD1619B 4-core 1.7 GHz, 1 GB DDR4; 16.31 W access / 4 W HDD hibernation; 18.2 dB(A); 2-year warranty (extendable to 4)
findings.note: Noise was measured fully loaded with Seagate 2TB ST2000VN000 drives at idle. The power footnote does not name the drives. Same CPU and RAM as the DS124, so streaming headroom is the same. The second bay adds about 5.6 W at access (16.31 − 10.69).

findings.label: What Infuse needs from the share (Firecore)
findings.value: SMB, NFS, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, FTPES, UPnP, DLNA or WebDAV; library features unavailable over UPnP/DLNA; SMB3 transport encryption can lower performance
findings.source_title: Streaming From a Mac, PC, or NAS – Firecore Support
findings.note: The rival page sets no NAS hardware requirement and gives no speed or bitrate figure. That missing figure is what the normalisation in this angle fills.
